title: BDD, ADR, PRD, WTF: Capturing Decisions for Humans and AI Alike — Michal Cichra, Safe Intelligence
talk_summary: Michal Cichra argues that agents and humans both suffer from limited context, so decisions must be captured in durable artifacts (ADRs, PRDs, BDD/Cucumber specs, design-system docs) and then enforced mechanically via git hooks, CI, linters, and architecture/import rules that link failures back to the governing document. He wraps this in a single generic agent loop (work → push → feedback → iterate) with skill-specific focus, and claims context compaction is survivable because the important rules get re-looked-up.

takeaways.technique: Enforce rules mechanically, link failures to the rationale doc
takeaways.what_they_do: Linters/architecture checks fail the commit and point the agent back to the ADR explaining why the rule exists and how to fix it, so the agent reads the doc and iterates instead of a human arguing style in review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tool will tell you that this is the rule. Why are you doing this? And how are you supposed to fix it?

takeaways.technique: Executable BDD specs as the reviewable layer between PRD and tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Cucumber-style human-readable scenarios are parsed and executed as code, linked to PRDs and critical user journeys, giving a readable, executable spec that closes the spec-driven-development validation gap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: One thing harder than reading an AI code is reading AI tests.

takeaways.technique: ADRs as scoped, enforceable architecture rules
takeaways.what_they_do: Each ADR records the why, the enforcement mechanism, and which files/folders it concerns; import-linting enforces layering (e.g. no DB access from templates or e2e tests) so classes of bugs are prevented rather than re-found.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You cannot keep finding them. You need to prevent them entirely.
takeaways.numbers: ~50 ADRs cited defining the product architecture

takeaways.what_they_do: Same work→push→feedback→iterate loop for all tasks, but skills switch focus: ADR skill looks up relevant ADRs and affected code, PRD skill likewise, UI skill skips checks and iterates in a browser, test skill selects tests by coverage/file changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that loop is the same, but what changes is the focus of the loop

takeaways.what_they_do: A test skill identifies which tests to run from code coverage and changed files, running a focused slice of the suite rather than everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we run just a focused part of the suite and not the entire suite

takeaways.technique: Design-system docs + previews as agent-readable UI contract
takeaways.what_they_do: Document component rules (e.g. one primary button per page), provide rendered previews/snippets agents can see, and enforce no-inline-styles so UI stays consistent and composable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: design system and pattern library are the way to build consistent UIs. Like that was the way before AI and it is the way now.
